:::{#lem-countable-additivity-empty}
#### Countable additivity and the empty set

If $\measure$ is a [countably additive](#def-countable-additivity) function
on a [$\sigma$-algebra](#def-sigma-algebra) $\salg$,
then $\measure(\emptyset) = 0$ or $\measure(\emptyset) = \infty$.

:::

::: proof

The set $\emptyset = S \setminus S$ is in $\salg$,
as the complement of $S$,
and the sequence $\emptyset, \emptyset, \ldots$ is pairwise disjoint with union $\emptyset$, so:

$$
\ba
\measure(\emptyset)
&= \measure\paren{\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} \emptyset}
&& \text{(the union of copies of } \emptyset \text{ is } \emptyset \text{)} \\
&= \sumto{i}{\infty} \measure(\emptyset)
&& \text{(countable additivity)}
\ea
$$

If $\measure(\emptyset) = c$ for a finite $c > 0$,
the right-hand side is $c + c + \cdots = \infty \neq c$,
a [contradiction](notation.qmd#def-proof-by-contradiction).
So $\measure(\emptyset)$ is 0 or $\infty$.

:::
